| [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 | Promotion is audited in small persisted batches, ranked by expected yield, with decisions recorded apart from status changes | The owner's procedure of 2026-10-19 for finding entries whose evidence has outgrown their status. Candidates are triaged from metadata by a rubric that sets review order and never standing. They are reviewed five at a time, and each review ends in one of six dispositions with a specific blocker. Every step is persisted in record/promotion-audit/: a versioned queue.yaml with a hand-off block, one decision file per candidate, and one file per batch. A check keeps the queue and the decision files in step. Status changes go in separate pull requests of at most three entries. Rejected: one large audit held in a conversation, which is lost when the session is; a queue derived only from the decision files, which cannot say what is in progress; and promoting in the same step as reviewing. | Active |
| [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) | A QUESTION is Answered by an Active CLAIM or THEORY, and a partly answered question is split into an Answered child and a narrowed Open parent | An Active THEORY is the record's current account, so it can answer a QUESTION as an Active CLAIM can. A CLAIM is not filed only to restate what a reading already establishes. A question is Answered when its Active answerers, alone or together, answer it as posed and in its full scope. When they answer only part of it, the answered part is filed as a child QUESTION that refines the parent and is marked Answered. The parent is reworded to what is left and stays Open. Rejected: requiring an Active CLAIM, which makes the record assert in its own voice what it relies on others to justify; marking a partly answered question Answered; and reframing the parent into new questions. | Active |
| [ADR-051](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-051.md) | A CASE names where the record got it: `reported_in` links it to the work, reading or account that reports it | A documented CASE usually comes from somewhere: a paper that reports a study, a reading that describes an episode, an account whose result the case records. The record had no field for that. A CASE could support a CLAIM but not point to a LIT, NOTE or THEORY, so its provenance lived in prose. At the owner's direction (2026-10-23), CASE gains `reported_in`, naming LITs, NOTEs and THEORYs, with the converse `reports` on each. It records provenance, not support. | Active |
